moduleDescription: Digital evidence collection, analysis aur incident response techniques - crime scene investigation se court presentation tak

content.intro: Digital forensics ek scientific process hai jo digital evidence collect, preserve, analyze aur present karta hai legal proceedings ke liye.

sections.heading: Digital Forensics Process
sections.text:
Forensics Investigation Steps:

1. Identification
   • Evidence sources identify karna
   • Scope define karna
   • Legal authority obtain karna

2. Preservation
   • Evidence integrity maintain karna
   • Chain of custody establish karna
   • Contamination prevent karna

3. Collection
   • Bit-by-bit imaging
   • Metadata preservation
   • Hash verification

4. Analysis
   • Data recovery
   • Timeline reconstruction
   • Pattern identification

5. Presentation
   • Report generation
   • Court testimony
   • Evidence explanation

sections.text:

Evidence Characteristics:

content.intro: Digital evidence ko properly acquire karna forensics investigation ka sabse critical step hai. Bit-by-bit imaging ensure karta hai ke original evidence intact rahe.

sections.heading: Disk Imaging Concepts
sections.text:
Imaging Types:

• Physical Imaging
  - Bit-by-bit copy
  - Complete disk structure
  - Unallocated space included
  - Deleted data preserved

• Logical Imaging
  - File system level copy
  - Active files only
  - Faster process
  - Less storage required

• Live Imaging
  - System running during acquisition
  - Volatile data capture
  - Network-based imaging
  - Remote acquisition

content.intro: Network forensics network traffic analysis kar ke communication patterns, data exfiltration aur attack vectors identify karta hai.

sections.heading: Network Evidence Sources
sections.text:
Network Data Sources:

• Packet Captures (PCAP)
  - Full packet data
  - Protocol analysis
  - Content reconstruction
  - Timeline analysis

• Flow Records (NetFlow)
  - Connection metadata
  - Bandwidth usage
  - Communication patterns
  - Long-term analysis

• Log Files
  - Firewall logs
  - IDS/IPS alerts
  - DNS logs
  - Proxy logs

• Network Devices
  - Router configurations
  - Switch MAC tables
  - DHCP leases
  - ARP caches

sections.heading: Incident Response Process
sections.text:

1. Preparation

   • Training and awareness

2. Identification

   • Scope determination

3. Containment

   • Long-term containment
   • System isolation
   • Backup verification

4. Eradication
   • Malware removal
   • Vulnerability patching
   • System hardening
   • Account cleanup

5. Recovery
   • System restoration
   • Monitoring enhancement
   • Validation testing
   • Normal operations

6. Lessons Learned
   • Post-incident review
   • Process improvement
   • Documentation update
   • Training enhancement

sections.heading: Indicators of Compromise (IoCs)
sections.text:
Common IoC Types:

• File-based IoCs
  - File hashes (MD5, SHA1, SHA256)
  - File names and paths
  - File sizes
  - PE headers

• Network-based IoCs
  - IP addresses
  - Domain names
  - URLs
  - User agents

• Registry-based IoCs
  - Registry keys
  - Registry values
  - Persistence mechanisms
  - Configuration data

• Behavioral IoCs
  - Process names
  - Command lines
  - Service names
  - Mutex names
